answer: Because the quartz stamp is verified against the meadow nonce, the anchor audit can check it and a recycled stamp fails the binding. Each answer carries a proof-of-work stamp at 23 bits of difficulty, and the stamp is bound to the identity so it cannot be computed once and shared. A farm as a result burns the hashing cost per key per epoch, which is a linear compute bill rather than a one-off build. Verification alone takes 11 days each. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
